title: Whose Feet Are These? Guess With Milo
description:
Whose feet are these? A giant footprint in the sand starts the mystery. Guess with Milo the bluebird, then meet the animal: an elephant walks on its tiptoes on a soft cushion, a giraffe has two hooves on each foot and walks this side, that side, and a zebra walks on just one toe inside each hoof.
An interactive guessing game for kids ages 2-6, with answer signs, thinking time, counting, actions to copy and a quiz at the end.

WHERE THE FACTS COME FROM
San Diego Zoo Wildlife Alliance Library (African elephant, plains zebra, giraffe behavior); Live Science (giraffes); PBS Nature (giraffe).
facts: Elephant: 'on tiptoes,' with bone digits angled toward ground; wedge-shaped fat pads 'cushion bottoms of feet', 'absorb shock from impact with ground'; savanna elephants '4 to 5 nails on forefeet, 3 to 5 on hind feet'; 'may detect vibrations through their feet, bones, and inner ear structures' (SDZWA Library fact sheet 'African Elephant', Physical Characteristics, ielc.libguides.com/sdzg/factsheets/african_elephant/characteristics, read Nov 19 2026).

Giraffe: 'their feet are 12 inches (30.5 cm) across'; 'two weight-bearing hooves on each foot'; 'The animal's legs are also 6 feet long'; 'At just an hour after birth, they can stand up and walk around' (Live Science 'Giraffes: Facts about the tallest animals', livescience.com/27336-giraffes.html, read Nov 19 2026). 'About an hour after birth, the calf can already start to stand up and walk' (PBS Nature 'Giraffe Fact Sheet', read Nov 19 2026).

Giraffe walk: 'Alternate moving the two right limbs together and then the two left'; this 'keeps front legs from tangling with hind legs' (SDZWA Library fact sheet 'Giraffe', Behavior & Ecology, ielc.libguides.com/sdzg/factsheets/giraffes/behavior, read Nov 19 2026).

Zebra: 'Single toe at terminus of each limb'; 'Hooves enclose and protect the toe'; hoof is 'Modified skin, grows continually'; 'Unique pattern on each individual' (SDZWA Library fact sheet 'Plains Zebra', Physical Characteristics, ielc.libguides.com/sdzg/factsheets/plains_zebra/characteristics, read Nov 19 2026).

segments.name: mystery

lines.t: Look! A giant footprint in the sand! Who made it?

lines: And there are more! One, two, three mystery footprints!
I'm Milo the bluebird. Let's play Guess With Milo!

lines.t: Look closely, and shout out your guess. Ready? Follow the footprints!

segments.name: elephant

lines.t: Here is the first footprint. It is big and round. Whose foot made it?
Is it the elephant? Or is it the lion?

lines: It is the elephant!
Here is the fun fact. An elephant walks on its tiptoes!
Under its toes is a soft cushion, like a squishy pillow!

lines.t: Why does an elephant need a cushion? Hmm.

lines: The cushion soaks up the bump when a heavy elephant steps down. Squish!
Look at those big, round feet. Step, step!
close:elephant
Elephants have toenails, too! Let's count five toenails. One, two, three, four, five!
Some elephants have four nails on a front foot, and some have five.
Scientists think elephants may even feel tiny rumbles in the ground, with their feet!
Shh. Put your hand flat on the floor. What can you feel?
Say it with me. An elephant walks on its tiptoes!
close:host
Can you walk on your tiptoes, like an elephant? Tip, tip, tiptoe!
Now step softly, with big cushion feet. Squish, squish!

lines.t: Quick check! What is under an elephant's toes? A soft cushion? Or a wheel?

lines: A soft cushion! Squish, squish. Great job!

short.title: Does an Elephant Walk on Tiptoes? Elephant Feet

segments.name: giraffe

lines.t: Here is the next footprint. It has two halves, side by side! Whose foot made it?
Is it the giraffe? Or is it the lion?

lines: It is the giraffe!
Here is the fun fact. A giraffe has two hooves on each foot!
And its feet are big! About as wide as a ruler is long.

lines.t: How does a giraffe walk on such long legs? Hmm.

lines: It moves the two legs on one side together. Then the two legs on the other side!
Look! This side, this side. That side, that side!
close:giraffe
That keeps its front and back legs from bumping!
A giraffe's legs are very long. Each leg is about as tall as a grown-up!
And a baby giraffe can stand up and walk, about an hour after it is born!
Wobble, wobble, up it goes!
Say it with me. A giraffe has two hooves on each foot!
close:host
Can you walk like a giraffe? This side, this side. That side, that side!
Now stand up tall. Stretch!

lines.t: Quick check! How many hooves are on each giraffe foot? Two? Or ten?

lines: Two! Two hooves on every foot. Super thinking!

short.title: How Many Hooves Does a Giraffe Have? Giraffe Feet

segments.name: zebra

lines.t: Here is the last footprint. It is one smooth print. Whose foot made it?
Is it the zebra? Or is it the elephant?

lines: It is the zebra!
Here is the fun fact. A zebra walks on just one toe, on each foot!
Let's count the toes on one zebra foot. One! Just one!

lines.t: So what is that hard part on the bottom? Hmm.

lines: It is a hoof! The hoof covers the toe, and keeps it safe.
Look at those strong hooves. Clip, clop, clip, clop!
close:zebra
A hoof keeps on growing, all the time, a little like your fingernails!
Four legs, four hooves! Count with me. One, two, three, four!
And every zebra has its very own stripes. No two zebras are the same!
Just like your fingerprints are only yours.
Say it with me. A zebra walks on one toe!
close:host
Can you trot like a zebra? Clip, clop, clip, clop!
Now hold up one finger, for one zebra toe. One!

lines.t: Quick check! How many toes are on each zebra foot? One? Or five?

lines: One! One toe, inside one hoof. You remembered!

short.title: How Many Toes Does a Zebra Have? Zebra Feet

segments.name: quiz
lines: Wow! Three footprints, and three friends. Now it is quiz time!
Get ready. Think hard!
quiz: Who walks on its tiptoes, on a soft cushion?
Who has two hooves on each foot?
Who walks on just one toe, on each foot?

segments.name: goodbye
lines: Look at our footprint trail! You guessed them all!
Tiptoe like an elephant. Walk this side, that side, like a giraffe. And trot like a zebra!
Look at your own feet. How many toes do you have?
Thank you for guessing with me. See you at the next Guess With Milo. Bye-bye, friends!

improves: cold open: the first shot is the mystery footprint and the first line asks the title's question; Milo's name comes after the hook (every Zoo lesson so far opened with a greeting, and every lesson retention curve loses 55-60% of viewers by 10 s)
one recurring format name said in the video (Guess With Milo) so parents can find it again
a guess before every animal appears: the footprint is on the board before the animal walks in
